text:
Anya Patel: Heads up — bulk SCIM sync for AcmeCorp is failing with 429 rate limits from Azure AD. Job stops after ~300 users, response contains Retry-After: 45. Provisioner leaves users in PENDING and we end up with partial state.

Sam Ortiz: Ugh. Azure AD throttles bulk ops hard. Two immediate mitigations: 1) honor Retry-After and queue retries with exponential backoff + jitter, 2) drop batch size (current is 200) to something like 25-50.

Jorge Alvarez: Can we confirm this is throttling and not token expiry or KMS errors? Any 401/403 mixed in logs? Also double-check if recent RBAC changes on the service principal reduced its quota or role.

Anya Patel: Logs excerpt: ```POST /scim/v2/BulkRequest  HTTP/1.1
Host: graph.microsoft.com
Authorization: Bearer ***
--- response ---
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 45
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": { "code":"TooManyRequests", "message":"Request limits reached." } }```
No 401/403. Service principal unchanged in IAM.

Security Oncall: Priority: we need auditability and a safe reconciliation path. Partial provisioning can cause role-assignment drift if we retry naively. Action items: (A) run reconciliation that is idempotent and logs each create/update attempt to our audit S3 bucket, (B) add incident tag so customer-success can notify the customer, (C) check if any admin-level roles were assigned during the window.

Sam Ortiz: For the retry strategy: implement exponential backoff with base 2s, max backoff 5m, and randomized jitter. Also respect Retry-After header if present (use header value as minimum backoff). Add circuit-breaker to pause and escalate if 429 rate > threshold for 10m.

Jorge Alvarez: From infra perspective we should add a quick mitigation: reduce batch to 25 and switch to delta pagination (don't send full bulk for very large orgs). That will reduce burst rate and should avoid the 429.

Security Oncall: Also add explicit audit entries for "attempted_provision", "received_429", and "reconcile_run" with correlation_id so we can tie customer-visible state to internal attempts. Retention: keep provision attempts for 90 days for compliance.

idp-bot: FYI Azure doc: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/throttling -- they recommend honoring Retry-After, reducing request rate, and using the delta API for larger syncs.

infra-bot: Created alert scim.bulk.429 at pager threshold 10 events/min, created ticket ENGINFRA-342 to implement backoff and queue. Prod rollout plan: feature flag + canary in dev then 10% traffic for 24h.

Sam Ortiz: Also consider making provisioning idempotent by using client-specified externalId and doing PUT semantics where possible — so retries are safe. Add per-resource dedupe via immutable external id.

Anya Patel: Immediate plan: I will reduce batch to 25 and re-run the reconciliation job now. I'll attach logs to ENGINFRA-342. Security Oncall, can you start the incident record and notify CS for AcmeCorp?

Security Oncall: On it — creating INC-185, pinging CS and product. We'll also check audit logs for any role assignments.

Jorge Alvarez: Longer term: infra to add backoff+queue, product to add "bulk-safe" mode for large org imports, security to validate audit/event schema. Owners: ENGINFRA-342 (Sam), SEC-185 (Security Oncall), PRODUCT-211 (Product).

Anya Patel: Thanks team — I'll post updates in this thread after the reconcile run. :thumbsup:
